packs.label: Fractions · Part 1: What is a Fraction?
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on fractions: parts of a whole, numerator and denominator.

lesson.title: 1. Understanding Fractions (حِصہٕ کیاہ چھُ؟)
lesson.objective: To help students understand parts of a whole, identify top and bottom numbers, and read simple fractions.

concepts.simplified_en: The numerator is the top number in a fraction. It tells us how many equal pieces we have taken, eaten, or shaded.
concepts.explanation_target: کُنہِ چیٖزُک کژ حِصہٕ اَسہِ ہیتہِ یا کھیو، تَتھ چھُ شُمار کَرن وول ونان۔ یہِ چھُ لکیرِ پیٹھ کَنہِ آسان۔
concepts.example_en: If you divide a Kashmiri Tsochwor into 4 equal slices and give 1 slice to a friend, 1 is the numerator.
concepts.example_target: اگر تُہہِ اکھ ژۄچوَر ژورَن برابر حِصَن مَنٛز کاٹِیو تہٕ اکھ حِصہٕ دوستَس دِیو، تیلی چھُ ۱ شُمار کَرن وول۔

concepts.simplified_en: The denominator is the bottom number. It shows the total number of equal parts the whole thing was cut into.
concepts.explanation_target: کُنہِ چیٖزَس کئتؠ کُل بَرابَر حِصہٕ کَرنہٕ آمٔتؠ چھِ، تَتھ چھُ نِسبَت ونان۔ یہِ چھُ لکیرِ بون کَنہِ آسان۔
concepts.example_en: If a sweet Kashmiri apple is cut into 8 equal slices, the total number 8 is the denominator.
concepts.example_target: اگر اکھ کٲشُر ژوٗنٛٹھ چھُ اَٹھَن برابر قاشَن مَنٛز کٹنہٕ آمُت، تیلی چھُ ۸ نِسبَت۔

quiz.question_en: In the fraction 3/7, which number is the numerator?
quiz.question_target: کٔسِر 3/7 مَنٛز، کُس نَمبَر شُمار کُنِندہ (Numerator) چھُ؟

quiz.question_en: In the fraction 5/12, what does 12 represent?
quiz.question_target: کٔسِر 5/12 مَنٛز نَمبَر 12 کیا ہاوان چھُ؟

quiz.question_en: A baker divides a Girda into 8 slices. You eat 5 slices. What is the numerator of eaten slices?
quiz.question_target: کاندرَن کٔرؠ اکھ گِردٕ ۸ حِصَن مَنٛز تَقسِیم۔ تُہؠ کھؠو ۵ حِصہٕ۔ کھؠمِژ کٔسِرِ ہُنٛد شُمار کُنِندہ کیا چھُ؟

packs.label: Fractions · Part 2: Proper & Improper Fractions
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on proper and improper fractions: numerator less than denominator vs greater than denominator.

lesson.title: 2. Proper & Improper Fractions (صحیح تہٕ غٲر صحیح کٔسِر)
lesson.objective: To distinguish between proper fractions (less than 1 whole) and improper fractions (1 or greater than 1).

concepts.simplified_en: A proper fraction is less than 1 whole. The top number (numerator) is smaller than the bottom number (denominator).
concepts.explanation_target: صحیح کٔسِر چھِ اِکِس کھۄتہٕ لۄکِٹ آسان۔ اَتھ مَنٛز چھُ شُمار کَرن وول نِسبَت کھۄتہٕ لۄکُٹ آسان، مِثال: ۳/۴۔
concepts.example_en: If you have 1 Girda and eat 3 pieces out of 4, you ate 3/4 of a Girda (less than a whole Girda).
concepts.example_target: اگر تُہہِ اِکِس گِردَس مَنٛزہ ۴ حِصَن مَنٛزہ ۳ حِصہٕ کھیو، یہِ چھُ ۱ کھۄتہٕ لۄکُٹ، یعنی صحیح کٔسِر۔

concepts.simplified_en: An improper fraction is equal to or greater than 1 whole. The top number is bigger than or equal to the bottom number, like 5/4 or 7/3.
concepts.explanation_target: غٲر صحیح کٔسِر چھِ ۱ یا ۱ کھۄتہٕ بَڈ آسان۔ شُمار کَرن وول چھُ نِسبَت کِس بَرابَر یا اَتھ کھۄتہٕ بوڈ آسان، مِثال: ۵/۴۔
concepts.example_en: If each Girda has 4 slices, and your family eats 5 slices in total, you ate 5/4 Girdas (more than one whole bread).
concepts.example_target: اگر پرؠتھ گِردَس مَنٛز ۴ قاشہٕ چھِ، تہٕ گَرَس مَنٛز کھؠو ۵ قاشہٕ، تیلی کھؠو تُہؠ ۵/۴ (اکھ پورٕ گِردٕ تہٕ بیاکھ قاش)۔

quiz.question_en: Which of the following is a proper fraction?
quiz.question_target: یِمَن مَنٛز کُس اکھ صحیح کٔسِر (Proper Fraction) چھِ؟

quiz.question_en: Which of the following is an improper fraction?
quiz.question_target: یِمَن مَنٛز کُس اکھ غٲر صحیح کٔسِر (Improper Fraction) چھِ؟

quiz.question_en: Is 4/4 considered an improper fraction?
quiz.question_target: کیا 4/4 چھِ غٲر صحیح کٔسِر مَنٛز گِننہٕ یِوان؟

packs.label: Fractions · Part 3: Mixed Fractions
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on mixed numbers and converting improper fractions to mixed fractions.

lesson.title: 3. Mixed Fractions (مِکلٕتھ کٔسِر - Mixed Numbers)
lesson.objective: To understand mixed numbers (a whole number combined with a fraction) and convert improper fractions into mixed numbers.

concepts.simplified_en: A mixed number combines a whole number and a proper fraction together. For example, 1 1/2 means one full item plus half of another.
concepts.explanation_target: مِکلٕتھ کٔسِر مَنٛز چھُ اکھ پورٕ نَمبَر تہٕ اکھ صحیح کٔسِر رَلِتھ آسان، مِثال: ۱ ۱/۲ (اکھ پورٕ تہٕ آدٕ)۔
concepts.example_en: At a Kashmiri wedding, boiling 2 and a half samovars of sweet Kahwa is written as 2 1/2 samovars.
concepts.example_target: خانٛدرَس مَنٛز زٕ پورٕ سَماوار تہٕ اکھ آدٕ سَماوار قَہوہ رَنُن چھُ ۲ ۱/۲ لؠکھنہٕ یِوان۔

concepts.name_target: غٲر صحیح کٔسِر مِکلٕتھ کٔسِرِ مَنٛز بَدلاوُن
concepts.simplified_en: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient becomes the whole number, the remainder becomes the new numerator, and denominator stays the same.
concepts.explanation_target: شُمار کُنِندَس کٔرِو نَصب نُما سٟتؠ تَقسِیم۔ حاصِلِ قِسمَت بَنے پورٕ نَمبَر، تہٕ باقٕیہ بَنے نَو شُمار کُنِندہ۔ مِثال: ۵/۴ = ۱ ۱/۴۔
concepts.example_en: If you have 7 half-apples (7/2), you have 3 whole apples and 1 half-apple left over: 3 1/2 apples.
concepts.example_target: اگر تُہہِ نِش چھِ ۷ آدٕ ژوٗنٛٹھ (۷/۲)، تِم بَنَن ۳ پورٕ ژوٗنٛٹھ تہٕ اکھ آدٕ ژوٗنٛٹھ: ۳ ۱/۲۔

quiz.question_en: Which of the following is a mixed fraction?
quiz.question_target: یِمَن مَنٛز کُس مِکلٕتھ کٔسِر (Mixed Fraction) چھِ؟

quiz.question_en: What is 5/2 written as a mixed number?
quiz.question_target: کٔسِر 5/2 مِکلٕتھ کٔسِرِ مَنٛز کِتھ کَن لؠکھنہٕ یِیہِ؟

packs.label: Fractions · Part 4: Equivalent Fractions
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on equivalent fractions: multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same number.

lesson.title: 4. Equivalent Fractions (بَرابَر کٔسِر)
lesson.objective: To find equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number.

concepts.simplified_en: Equivalent fractions look different but represent the exact same amount or value, such as 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8.
concepts.explanation_target: یہِ چھِ تِم کٔسِر یِم وُچھنہِ مَنٛز مُختَلِف چھِ آسان مَگَر اَصٕلَس مَنٛز چھِ اکھ بَرابَر قِیمَت تھاوان۔
concepts.example_en: Filling half of a kangri (1/2) holds the exact same coal as filling two quarters of it (2/4).
concepts.example_target: کَنٛگِیر آدٕ (۱/۲) بَرنہِ یِیہِ یا ژورَن مَنٛزہ زٕ حِصہٕ (۲/۴)، مِقدار چھُ بَرابَر۔

concepts.simplified_en: To find an equivalent fraction, multiply or divide BOTH the numerator and denominator by the same number.
concepts.explanation_target: بَرابَر کٔسِر بَناوَنہِ خٲطرٕ پَزِ شُمار کُنِندہ تہٕ نَصب نُما دۄشوٕنی اَکوی نَمبَرَس سٟتؠ ضَرَب یا تَقسِیم کَرُن۔
concepts.example_en: A saffron farmer dividing his field into 2 parts and working on 1 part is doing the same work as dividing into 4 parts and working on 2.
concepts.example_target: کۄنٛگ کِھت دۄن حِصَن مَنٛز ۱ حِصہٕ یا ژورَن مَنٛز ۲ حِصہٕ کٲم کَرُن چھُ ۱/۲ = ۲/۴ بَرابَر۔

quiz.question_en: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/3?
quiz.question_target: کٔسِر 1/3 ہِنٛدِ بَرابَر (Equivalent) کُس کٔسِر چھِ؟

quiz.question_en: Fill in the blank: 3/4 = ?/8
quiz.question_target: خٲلی جاے بٔرِو: 3/4 = ?/8

packs.label: Fractions · Part 5: Comparing & Adding Like Fractions
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on comparing fractions with like denominators and adding like fractions.

lesson.title: 5. Comparing & Adding Like Fractions (کٔسِر موازنہٕ تہٕ جمع)
lesson.objective: To compare fractions with the same denominator and add them by keeping the denominator same and adding numerators.

concepts.name_target: اَکوی نَصب نُما وٲلؠ کٔسِرَن ہُنٛد موازنہٕ
concepts.simplified_en: When the bottom numbers are the same, just look at the top numbers. The bigger top number is the bigger fraction: 5/8 > 3/8.
concepts.explanation_target: ییلہِ بۄنِم نَمبَر (نَصب نُما) اَکوی آسَن، بوڈ شُمار کُنِندہ بَناوان چھُ بوڈ کٔسِر۔ مِثال: ۵/۸ چھُ ۳/۸ کھۄتہٕ بوڈ۔
concepts.example_en: If Asif has woven 5/8 of a Pashmina shawl and Bilal has woven 3/8, Asif has woven more.
concepts.example_target: اگر عاصِفَن پَشمِینہِ شالُک ۵/۸ وۄو تہٕ بِلالَن ۳/۸، عاصِفَن چھُ زِیادٕ وۄنمُت۔

concepts.name_target: اَکوی نَصب نُما وٲلؠ کٔسِر جمع کَرُن
concepts.simplified_en: To add fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators together and keep the denominator unchanged: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5.
concepts.explanation_target: ییلہِ نَصب نُما بَرابَر آسَن، صِرِف شُمار کُنِندہ کٔرِو جمع، نَصب نُما چھُ سُہوی روزان۔ ۱/۵ + ۲/۵ = ۳/۵۔
concepts.example_en: If you drink 1/4 pot of Kahwa in the morning and 2/4 in the afternoon, you drank 3/4 pot in total.
concepts.example_target: صۆبحَس ۱/۴ پیا پیو تہٕ دَپھَرَس ۲/۴، کُل پیو تُہؠ ۱/۴ + ۲/۴ = ۳/۴۔

quiz.question_en: Which fraction is greater: 4/7 or 2/7?
quiz.question_target: کُس کٔسِر چھِ بَڈ: 4/7 کِنہ 2/7؟

quiz.question_en: What is 2/9 + 4/9?
quiz.question_target: 2/9 + 4/9 کیا بَنییہِ؟

packs.label: Fractions · Part 6: Word Problems & Real Life
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on real-life fraction word problems in Kashmiri contexts.

lesson.title: 6. Kashmiri Fraction Word Problems (عملی کٔسِر)
lesson.objective: To solve real-world daily life word problems involving fractions in Kashmiri settings.

concepts.name_en: Word Problems with Parts of a Whole
concepts.name_target: روزمرہ زِندگی مَنٛز کٔسِر ہِنٛزِ عملی مَسلہٕ
concepts.simplified_en: In real life, we use fractions when sharing food, measuring ingredients, and dividing tasks.
concepts.explanation_target: روزمرہ زِندگی مَنٛز چھِ اَسؠ کھیَن پؠن، باگاوَن، تہٕ کٲم تَقسِیم کَرنَس مَنٛز کٔسِر اِستِعمال کَران۔
concepts.example_en: Grandfather brings 12 walnuts. He gives 1/4 to Zooni. Zooni gets 3 walnuts (12 divided by 4).
concepts.example_target: بوڈٕ بابَن ہیتہِ ۱۲ دونٛٹھ۔ زوٗنِہ ہَس دِتُن ۱/۴، تَمِس مِلے ۳ دونٛٹھ۔

quiz.concept: Word Problems with Parts of a Whole
quiz.question_en: A box has 16 Kashmiri apples. You give 1/4 of them to your neighbor. How many apples did you give?
quiz.question_target: اِکِس پیٹی مَنٛز چھِ ۱۶ ژوٗنٛٹھ۔ تُہؠ دِیو ۱/۴ ہمسایَس۔ کٔتؠ ژوٗنٛٹھ دِتو؟

quiz.concept: Word Problems with Parts of a Whole
quiz.question_en: A baker bakes 20 Tsochwors. He sells 3/4 of them in the morning. How many Tsochwors were sold?
quiz.question_target: کاندرَن بَنٲوؠ ۲۰ ژۄچوَر۔ صۆبحَس کٔنؠ تَمؠ ۳/۴۔ کٔتؠ ژۄچوَر کٔنؠ تَمؠ؟

packs.label: Water cycle · Part 1: Journey of Water
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on the water cycle: continuous journey of water on Earth.

lesson.title: 1. The Water Cycle: The Journey of Water (آبُک چَکَر)
lesson.objective: To understand that water moves constantly between the ground and sky in a repeating cycle.
prerequisites: Water exists as liquid, ice and steam

concepts.simplified_en: The water cycle is the endless journey of water from Earth's surface to the atmosphere and back again. The water you drink today was once rain falling on ancient mountains.
concepts.explanation_target: آبُک چَکَر چھُ آبُک زٔمیٖنہِ پیٹھہٕ نَبَس کُن تہٕ نَبہٕ پیٹھہٕ واپس زٔمیٖنَس پؠٹھ اکھ لَگاتار سَفَر۔
concepts.example_en: Water in Dal Lake travels up to the sky as vapor, forms clouds, and returns as snow on the peaks of Zabarwan.
concepts.example_target: ڈَل جھیلُک آب چھُ باف بَنِتھ نَبَس کھَسان، اوبُر بَناوَن، تہٕ شِین بَنِتھ زَبَروَن پہاڑن پیٹھ واپس وَسان۔

quiz.question_en: Where does the energy that drives the water cycle come from?
quiz.question_target: واٹر سائیکل چَلاوَن وٲلؠ تَوانٲیی کَتہِ پیٹھہٕ یِوان چھِ؟

packs.label: Water cycle · Part 2: Evaporation
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on evaporation: heat changing liquid water into water vapor.

lesson.title: 2. Evaporation (باف بَنُن - Evaporation)
lesson.objective: To learn how sunlight heats water and converts it from liquid to invisible water vapor.
prerequisites: Water changes into steam when heated

concepts.simplified_en: When the sun warms up water in rivers and lakes, it turns into an invisible gas called water vapor that rises up into the sky.
concepts.explanation_target: آفتابُک گرمی چھِ آبَس تَتھاوَن تہٕ یہِ چھُ بے نِشان گیس (باف) بَنِتھ نَبَس کُن کھَسان۔
concepts.example_en: When you wash a wet Pheran and hang it under the sun, the water evaporates into the air and the cloth dries.
concepts.example_target: ییلہِ اَسؠ آفتابَس تَل نَم پھیرَن ترٛاوان چھِ، تَمِہ مَنٛزُک آب چھُ باف بَنِتھ نؠبَر نیران۔

quiz.question_en: What happens to liquid water during evaporation?
quiz.question_target: ایواپوریشن مَنٛز آبَس کیاہ چھُ گژھان؟

packs.label: Water cycle · Part 3: Condensation & Clouds
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on condensation: cool air turning water vapor into water droplets forming clouds.

lesson.title: 3. Condensation & Clouds (اوبُر بَنُن - Condensation)
lesson.objective: To explain how rising water vapor cools and condenses into cloud droplets and dew.

concepts.simplified_en: High up in the sky the air is cold. The invisible water vapor cools down and turns back into tiny water droplets, creating clouds.
concepts.explanation_target: نَبَس مَنٛز چھِ ترٛیشر (سَردی) آسان۔ ییلہِ آبُک باف تھود گژھان چھُ، سُہ چھُ شَبنَم تہٕ اوبُر بَناوَن۔
concepts.example_en: On a warm Kashmiri afternoon, a cold glass of Babribyol sharbat forms tiny water droplets on the outside.
concepts.example_target: شَربَت کِس تھدِ گلاسَس نؠبَر کَنہِ یِم آبٕچ قَطرٕ بَنان چھِ، سُہ چھُ کُنٛڈنسیشنُک مِثال۔

quiz.question_en: Clouds are formed due to the process of _______.
quiz.question_target: اوبُر چھُ _______ عَمَل کِنؠ بَنان۔

packs.label: Water cycle · Part 4: Precipitation (Rain & Snow)
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on precipitation: rain, snow, sleet and hail.

lesson.title: 4. Precipitation: Rain & Snow (رُود تہِ شِین)
lesson.objective: To understand different forms of precipitation when cloud water droplets become heavy.

concepts.simplified_en: When clouds become too heavy with water droplets, the water falls back to the Earth as rain or, in cold winter, as snow.
concepts.explanation_target: ییٚلہِ اوبُر واریاہ گۄب گژھان چھُ، آب چھُ رُود یا شِین بَنِتھ زمینَس پؠٹھ پؠوان۔
concepts.example_en: In the chill of Kashmiri winter, water vapor precipitates as white snowflakes blanketing Gulmarg and Pahalgam.
concepts.example_target: وَنٛدَس مَنٛز چھُ نَبہٕ پیٹھہٕ شِین پؠوان یُس گُلمَرگ تہٕ پَہَلگامَس سَفید چادَر چَڑھاوَن چھُ۔

quiz.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a form of precipitation?
quiz.question_target: یِمَن مَنٛز کُس پریسپیٹیشنُک قِسم نَہ چھُ؟

packs.label: Water cycle · Part 5: Collection & Glaciers
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on water collection, rivers and glaciers of Kashmir.

lesson.title: 5. Collection & Kashmir's Glaciers (آب جَمَع گژھُن تہٕ گلیشِیَر)
lesson.objective: To understand how melted snow and rainwater gather in rivers, streams, and lakes.

concepts.name_target: آب جَمَع گژھُن تہٕ کٲشِرؠ گلیشِیَر
concepts.simplified_en: Fallen snow packs onto mountains as glaciers. In spring, melted water flows down into streams like the Lidder and into River Jhelum.
concepts.explanation_target: پہاڑَن پؠٹھ چھُ شِین گلیشِیَر بَناوَن۔ سونٛتھ کِس موسمَس مَنٛز گَلِتھ آب لِدَر کولِ تہٕ وؠتھ (جہلم) مَنٛز وَسان چھُ۔
concepts.example_en: Rainwater and melted snow from the Pir Panjal range collect in the Dal Lake and flow down the Jhelum to feed our valley.
concepts.example_target: پِیر پَنٛجال پہاڑو پیٹھہٕ یُس آب وسان چھُ، تَمِہ سٟتؠ چھُ ڈَل جھیل بَران تہٕ وؠتھ پَکان۔

quiz.question_en: Where does most of the rainwater and melted snow eventually collect?
quiz.question_target: رُود تہٕ گَلمُت شِین کَتہِ جَمَع گژھان چھُ؟

packs.label: Atoms · Part 1: What is an Atom?
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on atoms: the fundamental building block of all matter.

lesson.title: 1. What is an Atom? (ایٹَم کیاہ چھُ؟)
lesson.objective: To define the atom as the basic unit of matter and understand its microscopic scale.

concepts.simplified_en: An atom is the smallest building block of all matter. Everything around you, including trees, copper pots, and air, is made of atoms.
concepts.explanation_target: ایٹَم چھُ کُنہِ چیٖزُک سارِوٕے کھۄتہٕ لۄکُٹ ذَرٕ۔ کائناتَس مَنٛز پرؠتھ چیٖز چھُ ایٹَمَن ہُنٛد بَنومُت۔
concepts.example_en: Just as a Kangri is woven from thousands of tiny willow twigs, every object is built from billions of tiny atoms.
concepts.example_target: جِتھ کَن اکھ کَنٛگِیر پۄتھَن ہِنٛدؠن لۄکٹؠن شَہَن سٟتؠ وۄنِتھ بَنان چھِ، تِتھ کَن چھُ پرؠتھ چیٖز ارباں ایٹَمَن ہُنٛد بَنومُت۔

quiz.question_en: What is the smallest basic unit of an element?
quiz.question_target: کُنہِ عُنصُرُک سارِوٕے کھۄتہٕ لۄکُٹ بُنیادی ذَرٕ کیا چھُ؟

packs.label: Atoms · Part 2: Protons & Neutrons in the Nucleus
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on the atomic nucleus, protons and neutrons.

lesson.title: 2. The Nucleus: Protons & Neutrons (نیوکلِیَس)
lesson.objective: To describe the central nucleus containing positively charged protons and neutral neutrons.

concepts.simplified_en: At the very center of an atom lies the dense nucleus. It houses positively charged protons and uncharged neutrons.
concepts.explanation_target: ایٹَم کِس بیٖچِس مَنٛز چھُ اکھ گۄب مَرکَز یَتھ نیوکلِیَس وَنان چھِ۔ اَتھ مَنٛز چھِ پروٹان تہٕ نیوٹران آسان۔
concepts.example_en: Think of a Kashmiri walnut: the dense inner core inside the shell is like the nucleus of an atom.
concepts.example_target: اکھ کٲشُر دونٛٹھ صوچِو: اَمِچ گُجی بیٖچِس مَنٛز بَنٛد چھِ، تِتھ کَن چھُ پروٹان تہٕ نیوٹران نیوکلِیَسَس مَنٛز آسان۔

quiz.question_en: Which subatomic particle carries a positive charge?
quiz.question_target: کُس ذَرٕ مُثبَت (Positive) چارج تھاوان چھُ؟

packs.label: Atoms · Part 3: Electrons and Shells
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on electrons, negative charge and electron shells.

lesson.title: 3. Electrons and Shells (الؠکٹران تہٕ مَدار)
lesson.objective: To learn how negatively charged electrons orbit the nucleus in energy levels.

concepts.simplified_en: Electrons are lightweight, negatively charged particles revolving around the nucleus at lightning speed.
concepts.explanation_target: الؠکٹران چھِ لۄکٹی مَنفی چارج تھَوَن وٲلؠ ذَرٕ یِم نیوکلِیَس کِس گِرد تیٖزی سٟتؠ چَکَر کَٹان چھِ۔
concepts.example_en: Picture honeybees buzzing rapidly around a fragrant saffron flower in Pampore. The flower is the nucleus, and the bees are electrons.
concepts.example_target: پامپور کِس کۄنٛگَس گِرد چَکَر کَٹَن وٲلِہ پۆمبُر صوچِو، پۆمبُر چھِ الؠکٹرانَن ہِش چَکَر کاٹان۔

quiz.question_en: What charge does an electron carry?
quiz.question_target: الؠکٹرانَس پؠٹھ کُس چارج آسان چھُ؟

packs.label: Atoms · Part 4: Elements & Periodic Table
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on chemical elements and atomic numbers.

lesson.title: 4. Elements & Periodic Table (عناصِر)
lesson.objective: To understand that each element has a unique number of protons and chemical properties.

concepts.simplified_en: An element is made of only one kind of atom. Copper, oxygen, and gold are all different elements with different numbers of protons.
concepts.explanation_target: عُنصُر مَنٛز چھِ صِرِف اَکوی قِسمُک ایٹَم آسان، مِثال: تام (Copper) یا سۄن (Gold)۔
concepts.example_en: A Kashmiri copper smith hammers a Samovar made of billions of pure copper (Cu) atoms.
concepts.example_target: کٲشُر کَنٛڈِل کار یُس تامُک ساموار ٹھوکان چھُ، سُہ چھُ تام کؠن پیوٗر ایٹَمَن ہُنٛد بَنومُت۔

quiz.question_en: Which element is commonly used to make traditional Kashmiri Samovars?
quiz.question_target: کٲشِرؠ رِوایَتی ساموار بَناوَنہِ خٲطرٕ کُس عُنصُر اِستِعمال گژھان چھُ؟

packs.label: Atoms · Part 5: Chemical Bonds & Molecules
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on molecules and chemical bonds.

lesson.title: 5. Chemical Bonds & Molecules (مالیکیول تہٕ بانٛڈ)
lesson.objective: To understand how atoms share or exchange electrons to form molecules like water and salt.

concepts.simplified_en: When two or more atoms join and bond together, they form a molecule. Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom form a water molecule (H2O).
concepts.explanation_target: ییلہِ زٕ یا زِیادٕ ایٹَم اکھ بَنٛدھَن (Bond) بَناوَن چھِ، تَتھ مالیکیول وَنان چھِ۔ مِثال: آب (H2O)۔
concepts.example_en: The salt in Kashmiri Noon Chai is made of sodium and chlorine atoms holding hands to form sodium chloride molecules.
concepts.example_target: نُوٗن چاے مَنٛز یُس نُوٗن (NaCl) چھُ، سُہ چھُ سوڈِیَم تہٕ کلورِین کین ایٹَمَن ہُنٛد رَلِتھ مالیکیول۔

quiz.question_en: How many hydrogen atoms are present in one water molecule (H2O)?
quiz.question_target: آب کِس اِکِس مالیکیول (H2O) مَنٛز کٔتؠ ہائیڈروجن ایٹَم آسان چھِ؟

packs.label: Photosynthesis · Part 1: How Plants Make Food
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on photosynthesis: how green leaves make food using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide.

lesson.title: 1. How Plants Make Food (غِذا بَناوُن)
lesson.objective: To learn the overall process where green plants turn sunlight, water and air into food.

concepts.simplified_en: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to make their own food. Leaves act like solar kitchens.
concepts.explanation_target: یہِ چھُ پَنَن مَنٛز غِذا بَناوَنُک طَریقہٕ۔ کُلِ چھِ آفتاب، آب تہِ ہَوا اِستِعمال کَرِتھ غِذا بَناوَن۔
concepts.example_en: A Kashmiri Haakh plant in a sunny kitchen garden grows faster because it makes more food with sunlight.
concepts.example_target: دٔجی مَنٛز ہاکھ تِتھؠ جایِہ اَصٕل بَڈان یِتہِ آفتابُک گاش اَصٕل پٲٹھؠ پیوان آسہِ۔

quiz.question_en: What energy source do green leaves use to produce food?
quiz.question_target: سَبز پَن غِذا بَناوَنہِ خٲطرٕ کُس طاقَت اِستِعمال کَران چھِ؟

packs.label: Photosynthesis · Part 2: Chlorophyll
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on chlorophyll: the green solar pigment.

lesson.title: 2. Chlorophyll: The Green Pigment (کَلوروفِل)
lesson.objective: To understand chlorophyll's role in absorbing light energy in plant cells.

concepts.simplified_en: Chlorophyll is the special green pigment inside leaves that captures energy from sunlight.
concepts.explanation_target: کَلوروفِل چھُ اَکھ سَبز رَنٛگ یُس پَننَن مَنٛز آسان چھُ تہٕ آفتابُک گاش جَذَب کَرنس مَنٛز مَدَد کَران۔
concepts.example_en: In autumn (Harud), chlorophyll breaks down, turning the Chinar leaves from deep green to bright orange and red.
concepts.example_target: بوٗنی ہِنٛد پَن چھِ ہاَرودَس مَنٛز کَلوروفِل کَم گَژھنہِ کِنؠ نِیول رَنٛگ تَرک کَران تہٕ موج گَژھان۔

quiz.question_en: Which pigment gives leaves their green color?
quiz.question_target: کُس پِگمینٹ پَننَن سَبز رَنٛگ دِوان چھُ؟

packs.label: Photosynthesis · Part 3: Stomata & Gas Exchange
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on stomata and gas exchange.

lesson.title: 3. Stomata: Leaf Pores (سُٹومیٹا)
lesson.objective: To learn how leaves take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen through microscopic pores.

concepts.simplified_en: Stomata are tiny microscopic pores on the underside of leaves that breathe in carbon dioxide and release oxygen.
concepts.explanation_target: سُٹومیٹا چھِ پَننَن ہِنٛدِ بۄنِمِہ طَرفہٕ لۄکٹی سوراخ یِم کُلِس ہَوا اَندر نِنہِ تہِ نؠبَر کَڈنہِ مَنٛز مَدَد کَران۔
concepts.example_en: Dust on apple orchard leaves near the road blocks stomata, making it hard for the tree to breathe.
concepts.example_target: ژوٗنٛٹھ کُلین ہِنٛدَن پَننَن پیٹھ دُود جَمَع گَژھنہِ سٟتؠ چھِ یِم لۄکٹی سوراخ بَنٛد گَژھان۔

quiz.question_en: What gas enters the plant through the stomata for photosynthesis?
quiz.question_target: فوٹوسِنتھِسِس خٲطرٕ کُس گیس سُٹومیٹا ذٔریعہٕ پَنَس اَندر گژھان چھُ؟

packs.label: Photosynthesis · Part 4: Water & Glucose
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on roots absorbing water and production of glucose.

lesson.title: 4. Water Transport & Glucose (آب تہٕ گلوکوز)
lesson.objective: To trace water transport from roots and examine glucose formation as chemical energy.

concepts.simplified_en: Roots draw water from the soil up through veins into the leaves. There, sunlight fuses water and carbon dioxide into sugar (glucose).
concepts.explanation_target: مُجِہ چھِ زٔمیٖنہِ پیٹھہٕ آب کَڈِتھ پَنَن کُن سوزان، جَتھ گاش آب تہٕ ہَوا رَلٲوِتھ کھؠن (گلوکوز) بَناوَن چھُ۔
concepts.example_en: The sweet sugar inside delicious Kashmiri apples was manufactured by leaves using sunlight and water.
concepts.example_target: ژوٗنٛٹھَن مَنٛز یُس مۆدُر رَس چھُ، سُہ چھُ پَنَن ہُنٛد بَنومُت گلوکوز۔

quiz.question_en: What is the food/sugar produced by photosynthesis called?
quiz.question_target: فوٹوسِنتھِسِس عَمَل مَنٛز پَنَن ہُنٛد بَنیومُت کھؠن کیا چھُ؟

packs.label: Photosynthesis · Part 5: The Oxygen Cycle
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on the oxygen byproduct and planetary oxygen cycle.

lesson.title: 5. Oxygen: The Life-Giving Byproduct (آکسیجَن)
lesson.objective: To appreciate how photosynthesis supplies all oxygen on Earth for humans and animals to breathe.

concepts.simplified_en: As plants make food, they release clean oxygen back into the atmosphere for humans and animals to breathe.
concepts.explanation_target: غِذا بَناوَنہِ پَتہٕ چھِ کُلِ نؠبَر صٲف آکسیجَن ترٛاوان یَتھ سٟتؠ اَسؠ پرؠتھ لَمحہٕ ساہ ہؠوان چھِ۔
concepts.example_en: The pine and chinar forests in Dachigam produce fresh, crisp mountain oxygen that keeps Srinagar's air pure.
concepts.example_target: داچی گام کؠن جَنٛگلَن مَنٛز کُلِ چھِ تازٕ آکسیجَن پٲدا کَران یُس کٔشیٖرِ ہِنٛز ہَوا صٲف تھاوان چھُ۔

quiz.question_en: What gas is released into the air as a byproduct of photosynthesis?
quiz.question_target: فوٹوسِنتھِسِس عَمَل مَنٛز نؠبَر کُس صٲف گیس کَڈنہٕ یِوان چھُ؟

packs.label: Environment · Part 1: What is Environment?
packs.subject: social
packs.source: Grade lesson on environment: land, water, plants, animals.

lesson.title: 1. What is our Environment? (ماحول کیا ہے؟)
lesson.objective: To define the environment and identify its living and non-living components.

concepts.simplified_en: The environment is everything that surrounds us: the land, air, water, plants, and animals.
concepts.explanation_target: ماحول سے مراد وہ تمام چیزیں ہیں جو ہمارے ارد گرد موجود ہیں جیسے زمین، پانی، ہوا اور جاندار۔
concepts.example_en: The Pir Panjal mountains, the Dal Lake, and Chinar trees form our environment in Kashmir.
concepts.example_target: کشمیر میں پہاڑ، جھیل ڈل اور چنار کے درخت ہمارے ماحول کا حصہ ہیں۔

quiz.question_en: What comprises our environment?
quiz.question_target: ہمارے ماحول میں کون سی چیزیں شامل ہیں؟
options: Both living and non-living things (جاندار اور بے جان دونوں)
quiz.answer: Both living and non-living things (جاندار اور بے جان دونوں)
quiz.answer_target: Both living and non-living things (جاندار اور بے جان دونوں)

packs.label: Environment · Part 2: Natural Resources
packs.subject: social
packs.source: Grade lesson on natural resources: water, soil, forests, air.

lesson.title: 2. Natural Resources (قدرتی وسائل)
lesson.objective: To identify renewable natural resources provided by nature.

concepts.simplified_en: Natural resources are gifts from nature that humans use to live, including fresh water, fertile soil, and forests.
concepts.explanation_target: قدرتی وسائل وہ نعمتیں ہیں جو قدرت نے انسان کو زندہ رہنے کے لیے دی ہیں جیسے پانی، مٹی اور جنگلات۔
concepts.example_en: We use the rich Kashmiri soil and mountain water to grow world-famous apples.
concepts.example_target: ہم کشمیر کی زرخیز مٹی اور چشموں کا پانی سیب اگانے کے لیے استعمال کرتے ہیں۔

quiz.question_en: Which of these is a vital natural resource for life?
quiz.question_target: ان میں سے کون سا زندگی کے لیے اہم قدرتی ذریعہ ہے؟

packs.label: Environment · Part 3: Human Dependence
packs.subject: social
packs.source: Grade lesson on human dependence on nature.

lesson.title: 3. Human Dependence on Nature (انسانوں کا انحصار)
lesson.objective: To understand how human survival depends directly on plants, animals, and clean climate.

concepts.simplified_en: Humans cannot survive without nature. Plants provide our food and oxygen, while animals give wool and milk.
concepts.explanation_target: انسان کا گزارہ قدرت کے بغیر ناممکن ہے۔ پودے ہمیں آکسیجن اور خوراک دیتے ہیں، اور بھیڑیں اون۔
concepts.example_en: In cold Kashmiri winters, we use wool from sheep for Pherans and willow wood for Kangris to keep warm.
concepts.example_target: سردیوں میں ہم بھیڑوں کی اون سے گرم پھیرن اور بید کی لکڑی سے کانگڑی بناتے ہیں۔

quiz.question_en: How do humans directly depend on plants?
quiz.question_target: انسان پودوں پر کس طرح منحصر ہیں؟
options: For food and oxygen (خوراک اور آکسیجن کے لیے)
quiz.answer: For food and oxygen (خوراک اور آکسیجن کے لیے)
quiz.answer_target: For food and oxygen (خوراک اور آکسیجن کے لیے)

packs.label: Environment · Part 4: Protecting Our Nature
packs.subject: social
packs.source: Grade lesson on conservation and protecting the environment.

lesson.title: 4. Protecting Our Environment (ماحول کا تحفظ)
lesson.objective: To understand why conserving forests, water bodies, and reducing waste is essential.

concepts.simplified_en: Protecting our environment means keeping our rivers clean, planting trees, and avoiding plastic waste.
concepts.explanation_target: اپنے ماحول کی حفاظت کا مطلب ہے ندی نالوں کو صاف رکھنا، شجرکاری کرنا، اور کچرا نہ پھیلانا۔
concepts.example_en: Keeping Dal Lake free of plastic and waste ensures clean water for future generations of Kashmir.
concepts.example_target: ڈل جھیل کو پلاسٹک اور گندگی سے پاک رکھنا ہماری خوبصورتی اور صحت کی ضمانت ہے۔

quiz.question_en: What is an effective way to protect our environment?
quiz.question_target: ماحول کو بچانے کا بہترین طریقہ کیا ہے؟
options: Planting trees and avoiding plastic (درخت لگانا اور پلاسٹک سے بچنا)
quiz.answer: Planting trees and avoiding plastic (درخت لگانا اور پلاسٹک سے بچنا)
quiz.answer_target: Planting trees and avoiding plastic (درخت لگانا اور پلاسٹک سے بچنا)

packs.label: Multiplication · Part 1: Repeated Addition
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on multiplication as repeated addition.

lesson.title: 1. Multiplication as Repeated Addition (لَگاتار جمع)
lesson.objective: To understand that multiplying numbers is adding equal groups together.

concepts.simplified_en: Multiplication is a fast way of adding equal groups. 3 groups of 4 walnuts is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 walnuts, written as 3 × 4 = 12.
concepts.explanation_target: ضَرَب چھُ اَکوی قِسمٕک گرُوپ لَگاتار جمع کَرنُک تیٖز طَریقہٕ۔ ۳ دفعہ ۴ دونٛٹھ جمع کَرُن چھُ ۳ × ۴ = ۱۲۔
concepts.example_en: If a farmer puts 5 walnuts in each of 4 willow baskets, he has 4 × 5 = 20 walnuts in total.
concepts.example_target: اگر اکھ زَمِیندار ۴ ٹوکرؠن مَنٛز ۵-۵ دونٛٹھ تھاوان چھُ، تَمِس نِش چھِ ۴ × ۵ = ۲۰ دونٛٹھ۔

quiz.question_en: Which repeated addition matches 4 × 3?
quiz.question_target: 4 × 3 خٲطرٕ کُس جمع مَیل کھؠوان چھُ؟

packs.label: Multiplication · Part 2: Arrays & Rows
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on arrays, rows and columns in multiplication.

lesson.title: 2. Arrays & Grids (قَطارَن مَنٛز گِنُن)
lesson.objective: To model multiplication using rows and columns in arrays.

concepts.simplified_en: Objects placed in equal rows and columns make an array. Rows × Columns gives the total number of items.
concepts.explanation_target: چیزن برابر قطارن مَنٛز تھاوُن چھُ اَرے بَناوَن۔ قطارن ضرب کٔرِو کالمَن سٟتؠ، کُل حِساب چھُ مِلان۔
concepts.example_en: Apples arranged in a wooden crate with 4 rows of 6 apples equal 4 × 6 = 24 apples.
concepts.example_target: پیٹی مَنٛز ۴ قطارن مَنٛز ۶-۶ ژوٗنٛٹھ تھاوُن چھُ ۴ × ۶ = ۲۴ ژوٗنٛٹھ بَناوَن۔

quiz.question_en: A baker arranges Kashmiri Girdas in 3 rows with 5 in each row. How many Girdas are there?
quiz.question_target: کاندرَن ترٛاوان چھِ ۳ قطارن مَنٛز ۵-۵ گِردٕ۔ کُل کٔتؠ گِردٕ چھِ؟

packs.label: Multiplication · Part 3: Multiplication Tables
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on multiplication tables and mental math.

lesson.title: 3. Times Tables & Patterns (پَہاڑٕ)
lesson.objective: To recognize number patterns and memorize essential multiplication facts.

concepts.simplified_en: Multiplication tables follow predictable skips. Multiplying by 10 always ends in 0; multiplying by 5 ends in 0 or 5.
concepts.explanation_target: پہاڑن مَنٛز چھِ نمبرن ہُنٛد نَمونہٕ آسان۔ ۱۰ سٟتؠ ضَرَب کَرنَس پؠٹھ چھُ ٲخِرَس ۰ یِوان۔
concepts.example_en: Each saffron flower has 6 purple petals. 5 flowers have 5 × 6 = 30 petals.
concepts.example_target: پرؠتھ کۄنٛگ پوشَس چھِ ۶ پَنکھڑی آسان۔ ۵ پوشَن چھِ ۵ × ۶ = ۳۰ پَنکھڑی۔

quiz.question_en: What is 7 × 8?
quiz.question_target: 7 × 8 کیا بَنییہِ؟

packs.label: Multiplication · Part 4: Kashmiri Word Problems
packs.subject: maths
packs.source: Grade lesson on multiplication word problems in Kashmir.

lesson.title: 4. Practical Word Problems (عملی ضَرَب)
lesson.objective: To solve two-step real-world problems in Kashmiri markets and crafts.

concepts.simplified_en: When shopping at the bazaar or selling handicrafts, multiplying unit price by quantity gives total cost.
concepts.explanation_target: بازارَس مَنٛز کُنہِ چیٖزٕچ قِیمَت تعدادَس سٟتؠ ضَرَب کَرِتھ کُل خَرچ لَبنہٕ یِوان چھُ۔
concepts.example_en: If 1 Kashmiri Girda costs 5 rupees, 6 Girdas cost 6 × 5 = 30 rupees.
concepts.example_target: اگر اکھ گِردٕ ۵ رۄپین مَنٛز یِوان چھُ، ۶ گِردَن ہُنٛد مُول چھُ ۶ × ۵ = ۳۰ رۄپیہِ۔

quiz.question_en: A shikara boatman charges 20 rupees per ride. He does 4 rides in the morning. How much money did he earn?
quiz.question_target: اکھ شِکارٕ وول ۲۰ رۄپیہِ چَلاوَن چھُ اِکِس چَکَر خٲطرٕ۔ ۴ چَکَر کٔرِتھ کٔتؠ رۄپیہِ کَمٲوَن تَمؠ؟

packs.label: Forces · Part 1: Push and Pull
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on force: pushes, pulls and motion.

lesson.title: 1. Pushes & Pulls (دَکہٕ تہٕ کَشِش)
lesson.objective: To define force as a push or a pull that changes an object's speed, direction, or shape.

concepts.simplified_en: A force is a push or pull on an object. Forces can make things start moving, speed up, slow down, or change direction.
concepts.explanation_target: طاقَت چھِ کُنہِ چیٖزَس دَکہٕ دِیُن یا پانہٕ کُن کَشِش کَرُن۔ اَتھ سٟتؠ چھِ چیٖز حَرکَت کَران۔
concepts.example_en: A boatman pulls the wooden paddle against the water of Dal Lake to push the Shikara forward.
concepts.example_target: ڈَل جھیلَس مَنٛز مٲنٛج چھُ چَپہٕ پانہٕ کُن کَشان تاکہِ شِکارٕ برٛونٛہہ کُن پَکے۔

quiz.question_en: What do we call a push or a pull on an object?
quiz.question_target: کُنہِ چیٖزَس دَکہٕ یا کَشِش کَرنَس کیاہ چھُ وَنان؟

packs.label: Forces · Part 2: Gravity
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on Earth's gravity and falling objects.

lesson.title: 2. Earth's Gravity (کَششِ ثِقَل - Gravity)
lesson.objective: To understand Earth's gravitational pull pulling all objects towards its center.

concepts.simplified_en: Gravity is the invisible pulling force of the Earth. It pulls everything downward towards the ground so we don't float into space.
concepts.explanation_target: کَششِ ثِقَل چھِ زٔمیٖنٕچ اکھ لۄکٹی مَگَر مَضبُوط کَشِش یۄس پرؠتھ چیٖز بۄن زٔمیٖن کُن کَشان چھِ۔
concepts.example_en: When a ripe apple breaks from a tree in Shopian, gravity pulls it straight down to the grass below.
concepts.example_target: شۆپیان کِس باغَس مَنٛز ییلہِ پۆکمُت ژوٗنٛٹھ کُلِ پیٹھہٕ کَٹان چھُ، سُہ چھُ بۄن زٔمیٖنَس پؠٹھ پؠوان۔

quiz.question_en: Why do dropped objects fall towards the ground?
quiz.question_target: تھاوِتھ ترٛاوِتھ چیز بۄن زٔمیٖن کُن کِیاہ چھِ پؠوان؟
options: Due to Earth's gravity (کَششِ ثِقَل کِنؠ)
quiz.answer: Due to Earth's gravity (کَششِ ثِقَل کِنؠ)
quiz.answer_target: Due to Earth's gravity (کَششِ ثِقَل کِنؠ)

packs.label: Forces · Part 3: Friction
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on friction, gripping and slipping.

lesson.title: 3. Friction & Gripping (رَگَڑ - Friction)
lesson.objective: To investigate friction between surfaces and how roughness affects motion.

concepts.simplified_en: Friction is the resistance force between two surfaces rubbing together. Rough surfaces create more friction; smooth ice creates very little.
concepts.explanation_target: رَگَڑ چھِ دۄن سَطَحَن درمِیان تِتھ طاقَت یۄس حَرکَتَس رُکاوَن چھِ۔ کھَردَرے سَطَحَن پؠٹھ چھِ رَگَڑ زِیادٕ آسان۔
concepts.example_en: Smooth shoe soles slip on frozen ice in winter because there is little friction; boots with deep treads grip the snow.
concepts.example_target: وَنٛدَس مَنٛز کُنگِری شِینَس پؠٹھ رَگَڑ کَم آسَن سٟتؠ چھُ اِنسان پِھسلان، مَگَر کھَردَرے بوٗٹ چھِ گرِپ بَناوَن۔

quiz.question_en: Why is it slippery to walk on frozen ice?
quiz.question_target: جَمِتھ شِینَس (Ice) پؠٹھ پَکُن کِیاہ چھُ پھِسلَندٕ آسان؟
options: There is very low friction (رَگَڑ چھِ واریاہ کَم آسان)
quiz.answer: There is very low friction (رَگَڑ چھِ واریاہ کَم آسان)
quiz.answer_target: There is very low friction (رَگَڑ چھِ واریاہ کَم آسان)

packs.label: Forces · Part 4: Weight vs Mass
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on mass vs weight.

lesson.title: 4. Weight vs Mass (مِقدار بَقابِل وَزَن)
lesson.objective: To distinguish between mass (amount of matter in kilograms) and weight (gravitational pull in Newtons).

concepts.simplified_en: Mass is the amount of matter inside you, which never changes. Weight is the gravitational pull on that mass.
concepts.explanation_target: مِقدار (Mass) چھُ کُنہِ چیٖزُک اَصلی مَواد یُس بَدلان نَہ چھُ۔ وَزَن چھُ زٔمیٖنٕچ کَشِش یۄس اَتھ مِقدارَس پیٹھ لَگان چھِ۔
concepts.example_en: A clay Kangri has the same amount of baked clay everywhere, but would feel 6 times lighter on the Moon because the Moon has weaker gravity.
concepts.example_target: کَنٛگِیر مَنٛز کُنڈَلُک مَواد چھُ سُہوی روزان مَگَر زوٗنہِ پؠٹھ آسِہ اَمِیُک وَزَن ۶ حِصہٕ کَم۔

quiz.question_en: Which quantity stays constant wherever you go in the universe?
quiz.question_target: کائناتَس مَنٛز کَتہِ ژلو، کُس چیٖز اَکوی قٲیِم روزان چھُ؟

packs.label: Electricity · Part 1: Electric Current
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on electric current, flow of electrons, circuits.

lesson.title: 1. What is Electric Current? (بِجلی کیاہ چھِ؟)
lesson.objective: To define electric current as the flow of electrons through a conductive pathway.

concepts.simplified_en: Electricity is the flow of tiny electric charges called electrons moving together through a wire like water flowing in a pipe.
concepts.explanation_target: بِجلی چھِ اصلَس مَنٛز تارَن مَنٛز الؠکٹرانَن ہُنٛد اکھ لَگاتار بَہاو یَتھ کَن نَلہِ مَنٛز آب پَکان چھُ۔
concepts.example_en: Water rushing down the Jhelum river spins giant turbines at the Uri powerhouse to generate electricity for Kashmir.
concepts.example_target: اوٗڑی کِس بِجلی گھرَس مَنٛز وؠتھ (Jhelum) ہُنٛد آب تَرکِش گھُمٲوِتھ کٔشیٖرِ خٲطرٕ بِجلی پٲدا کَران چھُ۔

quiz.question_en: What particles move through a metal wire to create an electric current?
quiz.question_target: تارَن مَنٛز کُس ذَرٕ پَکِتھ بِجلی بَناوَن چھِ؟

packs.label: Electricity · Part 2: Complete Circuits
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on closed vs open circuits.

lesson.title: 2. Simple Circuits & Switches (سَرکَٹ تہٕ سُوِچ)
lesson.objective: To construct a closed loop circuit with a battery, wire, switch and bulb.

concepts.simplified_en: Electricity needs a complete, unbroken circle (closed circuit) to flow. A switch opens the circuit to stop the flow and turn off the light.
concepts.explanation_target: بِجلی چَلنہِ خٲطرٕ چھُ پورٕ بَنٛد راستہٕ ضۆروٗری۔ سُوِچ دَبٲوِتھ چھُ راستہٕ ٹوٗٹان تہٕ بتؠ بَنٛد گژھان۔
concepts.example_en: When you press the button on your hand torch, you close the circuit so battery power lights up the small bulb.
concepts.example_target: ٹارچُک بَٹَن دَبٲوِتھ چھُ سَرکَٹ بَنٛد گژھان تہٕ بتؠ گاش دِوان۔

quiz.question_en: What happens when an electric switch is turned OFF?
quiz.question_target: ییٚلہِ سُوِچ بَنٛد (OFF) کَرنہٕ یِوان چھُ، تیٚلہِ کیاہ گژھان چھُ؟
options: The circuit is opened and current stops (سَرکَٹ ٹوٗٹان چھُ تہٕ بِجلی رُکان)
quiz.answer: The circuit is opened and current stops (سَرکَٹ ٹوٗٹان چھُ تہٕ بِجلی رُکان)
quiz.answer_target: The circuit is opened and current stops (سَرکَٹ ٹوٗٹان چھُ تہٕ بِجلی رُکان)

packs.label: Electricity · Part 3: Conductors & Insulators
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on electrical conductors vs insulators.

lesson.title: 3. Conductors & Insulators (موصل تہٕ غٲر موصل)
lesson.objective: To differentiate materials that allow electricity to flow freely from those that block it.

concepts.simplified_en: Conductors like copper and iron let electricity pass through easily. Insulators like rubber and plastic block electricity to keep us safe.
concepts.explanation_target: موصل (Conductors) مِثال تام تہٕ شِشتر چھِ بِجلی اَندر نِنہِ دِوان۔ رَبَڑ تہٕ پلاسٹِک چھِ بِجلی رُکاوَن تاکہِ اَسہِ کَرَنٛٹ نَہ لَگےِ۔
concepts.example_en: Electric wires in our homes have shiny copper metal inside to carry current, wrapped in colorful plastic outside for safety.
concepts.example_target: گرَن مَنٛز تارَن مَنٛز چھُ اَندر تام آسان مَگَر نؠبَر چھُ پلاسٹِک تاکہِ اِنسان صَحِیح سَلامَت روزِ۔

quiz.question_en: Which material is an insulator used to coat electric wires?
quiz.question_target: تارَن نؠبَر کُس مَواد غٲر موصل (Insulator) کِس طور لَگان چھُ؟

packs.label: Electricity · Part 4: Electrical Safety
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on safe use of electricity and fuses.

lesson.title: 4. Electrical Safety & Fuses (حِفاظَت تہٕ فِیوز)
lesson.objective: To understand home safety rules with electric heaters and the role of fuses.

concepts.simplified_en: Water is a conductor of electricity, so never touch electric appliances with wet hands. Fuses melt to cut off power if too much current flows.
concepts.explanation_target: آب چھُ بِجلی پَکناوَن، اَمِہ مۆکھ نَم اَتھن سٟتؠ سُوِچ کٔہِنٛزِ مہٕ چھُوِو۔ فِیوز چھُ زِیادٕ لۄڈ لَگنہِ پؠٹھ پِگھلان۔
concepts.example_en: Using heavy electric blowers and water geysers safely in Kashmiri winter requires proper earthing and fuses.
concepts.example_target: وَنٛدَس مَنٛز ہِیٹَر تہٕ گیزَر صَحِیح ارثِنگ تہٕ فِیوز سٟتؠ چَلاوِو تاکہِ شارٹ سَرکَٹ نَہ گَژھے۔

quiz.question_en: Why should you never touch electrical switches with wet hands?
quiz.question_target: نَم اَتھن سٟتؠ بِجلی ہُنٛد سُوِچ چُھوُن کِیاہ چھُ خَطرناک؟
options: Water conducts electricity and can give a shock (آب سٟتؠ چھُ کَرَنٛٹ لَگان)
quiz.answer: Water conducts electricity and can give a shock (آب سٟتؠ چھُ کَرَنٛٹ لَگان)
quiz.answer_target: Water conducts electricity and can give a shock (آب سٟتؠ چھُ کَرَنٛٹ لَگان)

packs.label: Matter · Part 1: Solid, Liquid & Gas
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on states of matter: solid, liquid, gas.

lesson.title: 1. Solid, Liquid & Gas (ٹھوس، آب تہٕ گیس)
lesson.objective: To identify the three states of matter by their shape, volume and particle packing.

concepts.simplified_en: Solids keep their fixed shape (like wood). Liquids flow and take the shape of their container (like Kahwa). Gases expand to fill any space (like air).
concepts.explanation_target: ٹھوس چھِ پَنُن شَکٕل قٲیِم تھاوان (کُلِ لَکٕڑ)۔ مائع چھُ بَہان (آب)۔ گیس چھُ سٲری جاے بَران (ہَوا)۔
concepts.example_en: A carved walnut wood table is a hard solid. The rushing cold water of Lidder is a liquid. The pine aroma in Pahalgam is a gas.
concepts.example_target: دونٛٹھ لَکٕڑِ ہُنٛد میز چھُ ٹھوس، لِدَر کولِ ہُند آب چھُ مائع، تہٕ جَنٛگَل مَنٛز ہَوا چھِ گیس۔

quiz.question_en: Which state of matter takes the shape of the container it is poured into?
quiz.question_target: کُس حالَت تَتھ بَرابَر شَکٕل ہؠوان چھُ یَتھ بَرَس مَنٛز یہِ ترٛاوَن چھِ؟

packs.label: Matter · Part 2: Melting and Freezing
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on changes of state: melting and freezing.

lesson.title: 2. Melting & Freezing (گَلُن تہٕ جَمُن)
lesson.objective: To understand how temperature changes cause matter to switch between solid and liquid.

concepts.simplified_en: Heating a solid causes it to melt into a liquid. Cooling a liquid below its freezing point turns it into a solid.
concepts.explanation_target: گرمی دِتھ چھُ ٹھوس گَلان تہٕ مائع بَنان۔ سَردی سٟتؠ چھُ آب جَمِتھ شِین بَنان۔
concepts.example_title: Dal Lake Freezing in Chillai Kalan
concepts.example_en: During Chillai Kalan in January, sub-zero cold freezes the surface water of Dal Lake into solid glassy ice.
concepts.example_target: چِلہِ کَلان مَنٛز بۄن ترٛیشر سٟتؠ چھُ ڈَل جھیلُک آب بۄن جَمِتھ شِیشہٕ ہِش شِین بَنان۔

quiz.question_en: What process turns solid ice into liquid water when heated?
quiz.question_target: شِین گرم کٔرِتھ آبَس مَنٛز بَدلَن کِس عَمَل کیاہ چھُ وَنان؟

packs.label: Matter · Part 3: Boiling & Evaporation
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on boiling and evaporation.

lesson.title: 3. Boiling & Vaporization (کھَولُن تہٕ باف)
lesson.objective: To explain the transformation of liquid into gas at boiling point.

concepts.simplified_en: When water reaches 100°C, it boils vigorously, producing steam bubbles that escape into the air as water vapor.
concepts.explanation_target: ییلہِ آب ۱۰۰ ڈِگری سینٹی گریڈَس پؠٹھ کھَولان چھُ، یہِ چھُ باف بَنِتھ نَبَس کُن کھَسان۔
concepts.example_en: When burning charcoal in a Samovar heats water to boiling point, white steam puffs out from the chimney top.
concepts.example_target: سَماوارَس مَنٛز چَکَن وٲلِہ قَہوہ کِہ نَلہِ مَنٛزہ یُس سَفید باف نیران چھُ، سُہ چھُ کھَولَنُک نَتیجَہ۔

quiz.question_en: At what temperature in degrees Celsius does pure water boil at sea level?
quiz.question_target: عام سَطَحَس پؠٹھ کٔتؠ ڈگری سینٹی گریڈَس پؠٹھ آب کھَولان چھُ؟

packs.label: Matter · Part 4: Particle Behavior
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on particle behavior in solids, liquids, gases.

lesson.title: 4. Particle Packing Inside Matter (ذَرَن ہِنٛز بَناوَٹ)
lesson.objective: To visualize how particles are tightly packed in solids, sliding in liquids, and bouncing freely in gases.

concepts.simplified_en: In solids, particles are locked tight and vibrate in place. In liquids, they slide past each other. In gases, they fly around with huge spaces between them.
concepts.explanation_target: ٹھوس مَنٛز چھِ ذَرٕ اکھ اِکِس سٟتؠ چِپکِتھ۔ مائع مَنٛز چھِ پَھسلان۔ گیس مَنٛز چھِ مۄکٕل پٲٹھؠ اُڈان۔
concepts.example_en: Like students packed shoulder-to-shoulder in morning assembly (solid) vs walking to recess (liquid) vs running in sports field (gas).
concepts.example_target: شُرؠ اسمبلی مَنٛز اکھ اِکِس سٟتؠ کھَڑا (ٹھوس)، گَرِ کُن پَکان (مائع)، تہٕ مَیدانَس مَنٛز دَووان (گیس)۔

quiz.question_en: In which state of matter are particles packed most tightly together?
quiz.question_target: کُس حالَتَس مَنٛز ذَرٕ سارِوٕے کھۄتہٕ نَزدیٖک تہٕ مَضبُوط چِپکِتھ آسان چھِ؟

packs.label: Solar System · Part 1: The Sun and Planets
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on the Sun, Earth and eight planets.

lesson.title: 1. The Sun and Eight Planets (آفتاب تہٕ اَٹھ سَیارٕ)
lesson.objective: To name and order the 8 planets revolving around the central star, the Sun.

concepts.simplified_en: Our solar system consists of the Sun at the center and 8 planets revolving around it: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
concepts.explanation_target: نِظامِ شَمسی مَنٛز چھُ آفتاب بیٖچِس مَنٛز تہٕ اَٹھ سَیارٕ اَمِس گِرد چَکَر کاٹان چھِ۔
concepts.example_en: Like spindles turning steadily around the wheel hub, all 8 planets orbit the glowing Sun in fixed tracks.
concepts.example_target: یَتھ کَن چَرخُک پہیہٕ مرکزَس گِرد پَکان چھُ، تِتھ کَن چھِ سَیارٕ آفتابَس گِرد چَکَر کاٹان۔

quiz.question_en: How many planets are there in our solar system?
quiz.question_target: سانہِ نِظامِ شَمسی مَنٛز کٔتؠ سَیارٕ (Planets) چھِ؟

packs.label: Solar System · Part 2: Planet Earth
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on Planet Earth: the blue planet with life and water.

lesson.title: 2. Earth: The Living Planet (سانی زٔمیٖن)
lesson.objective: To explain why Earth is the only known planet to support life, with liquid water and an atmosphere.

concepts.simplified_en: Earth is the third planet from the Sun. It has liquid water, an oxygen-rich atmosphere, and mild temperatures that allow plants, animals, and humans to thrive.
concepts.explanation_target: زٔمیٖن چھِ ترٛییِم سَیارٕ۔ اَتھ پؠٹھ چھُ آب، آکسیجَن تہٕ معتدل مَوسَم یَتھ سٟتؠ زِندگی مُمکِن چھِ۔
concepts.example_en: From space, the snowy mountains and green valley of Kashmir shine as part of Earth's vibrant living ecosystem.
concepts.example_target: آسمانہِ پیٹھہٕ کٔشیٖرِ ہِنٛز سَبز وادی تہٕ شِین لَگتھ پہاڑ چھِ زٔمیٖنہِ ہِنٛزِ زِندگی ہُنٛد حِصہٕ۔

quiz.question_en: What makes Earth unique compared to other planets?
quiz.question_target: باقٕیہ سَیارَن خِلاف زٔمیٖن کِیاہ مۆکھ خاص چھِ؟
options: It has liquid water and supports life (آب تہٕ زِندگی چھِ مۆجوٗد)
It is closest to the Sun
It is made of gas only
quiz.answer: It has liquid water and supports life (آب تہٕ زِندگی چھِ مۆجوٗد)

packs.label: Solar System · Part 3: Day and Night
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on Earth rotation causing day and night.

lesson.title: 3. Rotation: Day & Night (دوہ تہٕ رات)
lesson.objective: To explain how Earth's 24-hour rotation on its axis creates day and night.

concepts.name_target: زٔمیٖنہِ ہُنٛد چَکَر: دوہ تہٕ رات
concepts.simplified_en: Earth spins like a top on its axis once every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has daylight, while the side in shadow has nighttime.
concepts.explanation_target: زٔمیٖن چھِ پَننِس دُھرَس پؠٹھ ۲۴ گَنٛٹَن مَنٛز اکھ چَکَر کاٹان۔ یُس حِصہٕ آفتابَس سَمکھ آسِہ تَتھ مَنٛز چھُ دوہ بَنان۔
concepts.example_en: As Srinagar rotates toward the east, sunlight kisses the fort on Hari Parbat bringing morning to the valley.
concepts.example_target: سِری نَگَر ییلہِ مشرقَس کُن گُھمان چھُ، ہَری پَربَت کِس قِلعَس پؠٹھ صۆبحُک گاش پیوان چھُ۔

quiz.question_en: How many hours does Earth take to complete one full rotation on its axis?
quiz.question_target: زٔمیٖن پَننِس دُھرَس پؠٹھ اکھ پورٕ چَکَر کَرنَس مَنٛز کٔتؠ گَنٛٹہٕ لَگاوَن چھِ؟

packs.label: Solar System · Part 4: The Moon & Seasons
packs.subject: science
packs.source: Grade lesson on the Moon and Earth's orbit causing seasons.

lesson.title: 4. The Moon & Kashmir's Seasons (زوٗن تہٕ موسم)
lesson.objective: To explain how Earth's tilt as it orbits the Sun creates Kashmir's four distinct seasons (Sonth, Retakol, Harud, Wandh).

concepts.simplified_en: Earth orbits the Sun once a year (365 days). Because Earth is tilted, different parts receive more direct sunlight at different times, giving Kashmir its four seasons: Sonth (Spring), Retakol (Summer), Harud (Autumn), and Wandh (Winter).
concepts.explanation_target: زٔمیٖن چھِ آفتابَس گِرد اِکِس سالَس (۳۶۵ دوہ) مَنٛز چَکَر کاٹان۔ اَمِہ سٟتؠ چھِ کٔشیٖرِ مَنٛز ژور مَوسَم بَنان: سونٛتھ، ریٹھہٕ کول، ہاَرُد تہٕ وَنٛدٕ۔
concepts.example_en: The Chinar sprouts green buds in Sonth, provides cool shade in Retakol, glows fiery red in Harud, and rests bare in Wandh.
concepts.example_target: بوٗنی پَن سونٛتھَس مَنٛز پوٗٹھ دِوان، ریٹھہٕ کولَس مَنٛز نِیول سایہٕ، ہاَرودَس مَنٛز موج لعل، تہٕ وَنٛدَس مَنٛز آرام۔

quiz.question_en: What is the Kashmiri name for the autumn season when Chinar leaves turn red?
quiz.question_target: تَتھ موسمَس کٲشُر ناو کیاہ چھُ ییلہِ بوٗنی پَن لعل رَنٛگ ہؠوان چھِ؟
